page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the EPDSv5 family. It is powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a sustained frequency of 3.0 GHz. The instance features 32 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. It is equipped with 208.0 GB of RAM, providing 6.5 GB of memory per core, and includes 1229 GB of local SSD storage alongside Premium Storage compatibility.

Benchmark results place the E32pds_v5 in the average tier for most multi-core and memory operations. The system achieved a multi-core Stress-ng CPU score of 57247.25 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 13049.0, though its single-core Geekbench score of 1122.0 is categorized as weak. Memory performance is robust, with a read-only small-block cached bandwidth of 2231.95 GB/sec and a large-block uncached write speed of 77.64 GB/sec. Database operations are supported by a Passmark database score of 21161.56 and Redis SET performance reaching 41.96 million operations per second. However, large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model yielding poor performance at 2.43 tokens per second for text generation.

Utilizing ARM64 architecture allows the E32pds_v5 to deliver high resource density and power efficiency compared to traditional x86 alternatives. The combination of 208.0 GB of memory and a 1229 GB local SSD makes this instance well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, and web serving, where it achieves a static web serving throughput of 32.4 GB/sec. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or heavy AI model inference.
description: The Microsoft Azure E32pds_v5 is an ARM64-based virtual machine from the EPDSv5 family, featuring 32 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It is configured with 208.0 GB of RAM and 1229 GB of local SSD storage, with support for Premium Storage. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance delivers solid multi-core performance, as evidenced by a multi-core Stress-ng score of 57247.25 and a Passmark database score of 21161.56. While single-core performance and large-scale LLM inference are relatively weak, its high memory capacity and fast local storage make it highly efficient for memory-intensive applications, database operations, and high-throughput static web serving.
